text:
meera: Heads-up — ACME dedicated tenant (acct: acme-prod) opened a Sev2. They're seeing lots of 429s and token latency spikes since this morning after enabling 'extended-history' (long context). Customer report: ~30% of requests hitting 429s and tail p95 p99 latency up ~3-4x.

jess: yep, we flipped extended-history at ~08:10 UTC. It works locally but in prod we're hitting throttles. Logs show: 
`error: request rejected: kv_cache_evicted` repeatedly.

meera: Thanks @jess. I grabbed the rooftop metrics — KV cache size for their shard is at ~92% used and eviction rate jumped at 08:12. Looks like long contexts are causing frequent large KV entries and fragmentation.

alex: Can you paste the request pattern and an example request id? I want to pull trace.

jess: sample request-id: trace-0b7c9e; payload size: ~1.6M tokens window (they stream multiple docs into context). curl sample:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rw-long-8b","context": "<lots of text>", "session_id": "acme-ext-01"}'
```

meera: Repro steps I'm running on a staging pod: send 10 simultaneous long-context requests (single tenant) with ~500k token history each. Observed KV insert latency spikes and then immediate evictions, followed by 429 responses from the quota guard.

eng-bot: [alert] kv_cache_eviction_rate > threshold for tenant acme-prod on shard us-west-2-a (since 2024-11-20T08:12:30Z).

sam: Likely causes: huge KV entries + fragmentation + per-tenant cache quota enforcement stepping in. Two candidate mitigations: 1) temporarily increase KV allocation for that tenant (if Dedicated capacity has spare mem) OR 2) enable aggressive prefix compaction / baseline eviction policy for long contexts OR 3) route long-context traffic to a lower-cost fallback model with smaller window.

meera: I pulled heap/kv stats from their Dedicated pool:
```
kv_slots_total: 524288
kv_slots_used: 482912
avg_entry_size: 10.8KB
largest_fragment_chain: 68
evictions_per_min: 820
mem_fragmentation_ratio: 1.42
```

alex: Fragmentation ratio >1.3 is bad. Also seeing repeated small free segments not coalescing — sounds like allocator churn when large/variable KV item sizes are inserted. Could be exacerbated by our jemalloc config on that node type.

meera: Customer asked for quick remediation. Options:
- Short-term: bump tenant KV cap by 25% and temporarily throttle new long-context sessions (soft limit) to reduce write rate.
- Mid-term: change eviction policy to LRU-with-prefetch hint for long sessions and compact on eviction.
- Long-term: patch runtime to use size-aware slab allocation for KV to reduce fragmentation.

jess: short-term bump would be great. We need minimal downtime.

sam: I can flip the tenant cap if capacity available. @alex can you confirm node-level memory headroom? ops-bot: performing capacity scan...

ops-bot: scan result: dedicated-pool-usw2-a has 8% free GPU host RAM overall; bumping tenant cap by 25% will require migrating one small burst instance or enabling burst-swap which may impact tail latency for other tenants.

alex: Not ideal but doable as an emergency. Two caveats: (1) migration will cause a short scheduling window (~30s) and (2) if fragmentation remains, increased cap will be consumed quickly and we might still hit evictions.

meera: Plan: 1) Ask ACME to temporarily gate new long-history sessions (we can set header `X-ACME-Gated: true` or use per-route throttling) — Jess can you do that? 2) Sam to bump tenant KV cap + enable compaction flag on the tenant's shard. 3) Alex to collect jemalloc stats and core dump if eviction spikes persist. 4) Support to monitor 429 rate and rollback if cross-tenant impact.

jess: I've turned on gating on our side and paused new sessions.

sam: Bumping cap now and enabling compaction flag `kv.compact_on_eviction=true` for tenant acme-prod. Will post when done.

sam: Done — KV cap increased + compaction flag applied. Observing immediate drop in eviction rate. 429s reduced from 30% -> 6% in first 2 minutes. p95 latency trending down. :relieved:

meera: Great. alex, any action items for runtime patch?

alex: I'll dig into allocator metrics and run a repro with different jemalloc tunables. If we can reproduce fragmentation in a test harness, we can ship size-aware slabs. Creating a ticket ENG-RUN-1427 and assigning to runtime.

meera: Marking support follow-up: confirm with ACME after 24h and schedule dedicated runtime change. Also recommend they stagger large uploads and consider breaking context into referential chunks instead of single massive KV entries. I'll update the ticket with mitigations and logs.

jess: Thanks all — things look stable for now. Please keep me posted if anything changes.

meera: closing the incident after 24h monitoring window unless regressions. :white_check_mark:
